worker--distribution--pqa-analysis.md:
---
schemaVersion: 1
workerId: worker--distribution--pqa-analysis
domain: distribution
analysisId: pqa-analysis
pageKey: p_rsv_vs_distribution
label: PQA Analysis
definition: Identifies Hero SKUs (Q1 SKUs in PQA) and incremental sales opportunities from distribution by relating sales performance to weighted distribution.
aliases: [PQA, performance quadrant analysis, distribution opportunity analysis, Hero SKU, Hero SKUs, PQA Q1 SKUs]
routingPhrases:
  - distribution-push opportunities
  - PQA opportunities
  - relative sales versus distribution
  - incremental sales opportunity from distribution
  - incremental sales opportunity
  - incremental sales opportunities
  - distribution upside
  - hero SKU
  - hero SKUs
  - PQA Q1 SKUs
routingExamples:
  - Run PQA to find brands with strong sales but weak distribution.
  - Rank the largest distribution-push opportunities.
  - Plot relative sales value against weighted distribution.
  - Which are hero SKUs for Bayer in each partition in UK Womens Intimate Health?
  - Identify the Q1 SKUs in the distribution analysis.
  - Which SKUs have the largest incremental sales opportunities from closing distribution gaps?
  - Rank brands by incremental sales opportunity in the selected market.
nonRoutingPhrases:
  - ordinary sales ranking without distribution analysis
  - market segment size and share
  - quarterly growth comparison
  - Q1 calendar-quarter sales totals
  - historical sales change between periods
exclusions:
  - Does not provide a general category market overview.
  - Does not replace ordinary ranking when no distribution relationship is requested.
  - Does not treat historical sales growth or promotional causal lift as distribution-derived incremental sales opportunity.
  - Does not interpret Q1 alone as a PQA quadrant when the request refers to a calendar quarter.
metrics:
  - id: relative-sales-value
    label: Relative Sales Value
    aliases: [RSV, relative value sales]
    executionValue: rsv
    sourceFields: [sales, category_sales]
    description: Sales performance indexed relative to the applicable category benchmark.
    default: true
  - id: weighted-distribution
    label: Weighted Distribution
    aliases: [WD, distribution]
    executionValue: weighted_distribution
    sourceFields: [weighted_distribution]
    description: Sales-weighted measure of product availability.
    default: false
  - id: incremental-sales-opportunity
    label: Incremental Sales Opportunity
    aliases: [opportunity value, distribution upside, incremental sales opportunity, incremental sales opportunities]
    executionValue: incremental_sales_opportunity
    sourceFields: [sales, weighted_distribution]
    description: Estimated sales upside associated with closing a distribution gap.
    default: false
grains:
  - id: brand
    label: Brand
    aliases: [brands]
    dimensions: [brand]
    role: opportunity-item
    description: One PQA opportunity per brand within the locked market scope.
    default: true
  - id: sku
    label: SKU
    aliases: [product, products, item]
    dimensions: [sku]
    role: opportunity-item
    description: Product-level PQA opportunities when the configured page supports the requested scope.
    default: false
dimensions:
  - id: country
    label: Country
    role: filter
    pageFilter: country
    djangoFilter: country
  - id: category
    label: Category
    role: filter
    pageFilter: category
    djangoFilter: category
  - id: brand
    label: Brand
    role: breakdown
    pageFilter: brand
    djangoFilter: brand
  - id: sku
    label: SKU
    role: breakdown
    pageFilter: sku
    djangoFilter: sku
requiredInputs:
  - id: country
    field: country
    label: Country
    type: entity
    entityDimension: country
    cardinality: single
    description: Exactly one country is required for a PQA run.
  - id: category
    field: category
    label: Category
    type: entity
    entityDimension: category
    cardinality: single
    description: Exactly one category is required for a PQA run.
optionalInputs: []
configuredDefaults:
  metric: relative-sales-value
  grain: brand
executionLimitations:
  - Execution is bound to the configured PQA page and its validated evidence envelope.
  - Country and category must be locked catalog entities before execution.
  - Hero SKU membership uses the configured PQA Q1 classification; never invent quadrant thresholds.
  - Partition-level presentation requires partition information in the configured page evidence; report a limitation if unavailable.
routingLimitations:
  - Select when distribution performance, distribution-derived incremental sales, Hero SKUs, or the named PQA method is material to the request; the user need not name PQA explicitly.
  - Hero SKUs means Q1 SKUs in PQA, not an ordinary ranking of top-selling products.
  - Unqualified incremental sales may need semantic clarification if distribution opportunity versus historical change is unresolved.
---

# PQA Analysis

Use this worker for the configured relationship between relative sales performance
and weighted distribution. Its default interpretation is the relative-sales-value
metric at brand grain. A request for ordinary sales, growth, share, or category
ranking does not route here unless it also asks for the PQA/distribution-opportunity
method, including its registered Hero SKU business terminology.

Hero SKUs are Q1 SKUs in PQA. Preserve this classification and SKU grain when
forming the task; do not substitute top-selling products or calendar-quarter Q1.
For requests for Hero SKUs in each partition, preserve the per-partition output
requirement and use only classifications and partitions supported by the configured
page evidence. Missing support is a limitation, not permission to invent thresholds
or replace the PQA method with generic SQL.

Incremental sales opportunity means estimated upside from closing distribution
gaps. It is distinct from historical sales change and promotional causal lift.
These business terms establish analytical ownership without requiring the user to
name PQA. Hero SKU identification alone does not specify a metric; preserve the
planner's semantic review for omitted metrics rather than inventing one.

The worker requires one catalog-authorized country and one catalog-authorized
category. These inputs are stricter than any downstream SQL or page defaults.

# Ad hoc Data Analysis

Use this fallback for descriptive queries that an inspected specialist does not own.
Build a schema-grounded, read-only query through the generic query tool. Preserve
locked catalog scope and ask the planner semantic review to resolve any omitted
metric before execution.

Hero SKU identification and distribution-derived incremental sales opportunities
belong to PQA even when the question does not name that method. A generic sales
ranking or period delta does not answer those questions. If incremental sales is
ambiguous, resolve its intended meaning rather than assuming historical growth.

# Category Market Segments

Use this worker for descriptive category and market-segment comparisons, including
market size, value growth, share, structure, and curated white-space views. The
unqualified default is value sales at category grain.

The worker requires at least one catalog-authorized country and category. Both
inputs accept multiple values, subject to the selected execution contract.
